task.title: Page one-shot schedules sparsely by status through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/995 by exposing bounded schedule status scans as deterministic read-only JSON.
acceptance_criteria: Validate exact status, positive at-most-1024 scan size, and optional exact schedule-ID cursor before storage access.
Emit complete matching schedules and the kernel-owned nullable last-inspected continuation cursor.
Open only existing storage read-only and fail without partial stdout on selected-window corruption or storage errors.

attempts.diagnostic: The CLI rejected schedule status-page because the subcommand did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added CLI tests for sparse continuation, ordering, escaping, validation before storage, missing paths, and corruption isolation.

attempts.summary: Implemented and refactored the read-only adapter.
attempts.diagnostic: Implemented pre-storage status, size, and cursor validation, read-only kernel delegation, and compact continuation JSON.
attempts.patch: Implemented issue 995 in crates/vela-dev/src/lib.rs with CLI tests, ADR-0096, and scheduler documentation; independent review prompted ordering and escaping coverage.

attempts.diagnostic: A rate-limited false green was excluded; after cooldown, CodeRabbit command 73de27bd completed on exact head 4a0f25d with no actionable comments and zero unresolved threads.
attempts.patch: Kept auto-merge disabled until exact-head Rust CI and genuine review both passed.

outcome.summary: Issue 995 exposed bounded sparse schedule status paging while preserving kernel cursor and read-only authority.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate for pull request 996 exact head 4a0f25de51c99a37e065ab23e4dc226c161d82a0

lessons: Caller-owned filters, bounds, and cursors belong before storage access while continuation truth remains kernel-owned.
An empty schedules array with non-null next_after is valid progress, not terminal evidence.
The adapter adds no ambient clock, persisted cursor, lifecycle mutation, dispatch, permission, or execution authority.
